items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: They had him on trumpet, Emma Bauer on piano, me on banjo.

ctx.x: Around in that neighborhood? The only thing I remember, I remember there was a colored theater and there was one place we used to go, like I used to go eat. And you could drink like, you know, during probation days and get whiskey and things. But, yeah, when this fella Red came on the boat and work, well like I said, I was still around Memphis because I had gotten my hotel room and he and I feel like we were still on a good time. It wasn't long. So we went up with them one night for this particular place. I…
Budweiser? Was it near the Budweiser?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: not working, but I mean getting jobs with Emma Barrett and Paul Barberin and, uh, Noon and the Bazooka Man.

ctx.x: And when I came back, well, that's where I start, uh, working with, uh, not working, but I mean getting jobs with Emma Barrett and Paul Barberin and, uh, Noon and the Bazooka Man.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: Then they made it Sweet Emmons night, called it her band

ctx.x: That's the only reason why I went back on banjo, you see. Yeah. And like I said, I enjoyed Luce Band, and when I came back, like I said before, I lost my scene now after so. So Punch had a Sunday night date there, and he requested for them to hire me. So I stayed with that band. When Punch died, and there was some other trumpet player, and that's why. Then they made it Sweet Emmons night, called it her band, Pussy and Willie Humphrey, came in there and started playing. Now they're the top band today, because…
Yeah. And so you played some at Preservation Hall before you went up to Chicago?
